page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.metal-24xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 architecture. The hardware features 96 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARM Neoverse-V2 microarchitecture running at 2.8 GHz with single-threaded execution per core. Memory allocation includes 384.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. Cache layout consists of 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. The instance includes no integrated local storage and contains no discrete graphics accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded compute and data transfer capabilities. The 96 physical cores achieve top-decile performance in multi-core stress testing and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, alongside single-threaded bzip3 throughput that reaches the top 25%. Memory subsystem throughput ranks in the top 10% across cached and uncached block reads as well as large-block writes. Similarly, network-adjacent testing reveals exceptional results, placing redis SET operations and static web serving throughput in the top 10% bracket. Single-core compute and small-model text generation remain average or lower-tier, reflecting the density-focused scaling model of the ARMv9 cores.

Without onboard storage, deployments rely completely on external network-attached storage volumes, making the 300 Gbps baseline network interface critical to overall throughput. From an operational perspective, the bare-metal architecture removes hypervisor overhead, maximizing efficiency for dense, multi-threaded workloads. While single-thread execution speed is moderate, the high core count and massive memory bandwidth offer efficient resource utilization across enterprise container hosts, distributed databases, in-memory caching layers, and high-throughput network appliances.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gn.metal-24xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server based on 96 dedicated physical ARM Neoverse-V2 cores clocked at 2.8 GHz on the ARMv9 architecture. Configured with 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory, it provides a balanced 4.0 GB per core profile with top-tier memory bandwidth across both cached reads and uncached block writes. The platform includes no local disk storage and no GPU hardware, instead utilizing a 300 Gbps baseline network pipe to facilitate external storage access and massive node-to-node communication. Benchmark measurements highlight top-decile multi-core CPU performance, web serving throughput, and key-value cache operations, balanced against moderate single-core instruction processing. The absence of hypervisor layers yields predictable performance and high compute density, presenting an efficient hardware footprint for high-concurrency microservices, in-memory databases, and large-scale web infrastructure.
